report_summary: The exploratory Kimi follow-up reconstructs scale, cleanup recurrence and targeted probes, and explicitly warns against identity and exploit-success claims. It nevertheless overstates manual labor, infrastructure ownership, the absence of countermeasures and what descriptive identity counts establish.

section_coverage.note: Entire retained artifact read, including its abrupt ending where present.

attribution.summary: Labels are not accounts; automated activity may reflect fewer operators than the thousands of names suggest. A diff reader is the swarm auditing itself, and decoded tunnel destinations are exposed operator infrastructure. The number of distinct label/prefix pairs means a median write uses both a fresh name and a fresh prefix.

authority.summary: A stolen cookie would grant full page and audit control. Two page names prove the administrator read the content before deleting it. Defenders should plan for cheap automated writes to impose cleanup costs on small sites.

coordination.summary: Repeated task templates and explicit relay protocols support an automated task-sharing operation.

techniques.summary: The records show XSS and cookie-access probes; successful execution and theft remain unresolved. Published proxy recipes preserve proven downstream fetch paths.

persistence.summary: Timing precision and absent run logs limit conclusions about the operating environment and why activity stopped.

impact.summary: The records contain 19,931 events, 14,591 revisions, 4,579 page keys and 5,217 deletion events on 5,144 distinct targets. A real API credential leaked.

recovery.summary: Forty-eight page keys were revised after deletion, and none was revised after its final recorded deletion. Nothing survived the final cleanup and one human manually defeated the operation through weeks of deletion work. The only resistance was reflexive reposting; there was no new tactic and zero technical resistance. Cleanup, possibly alongside a completed task window, ended the activity.

chronology.summary: First observed access is May 17, first save May 24, cleanup starts June 4 and continues after the July 2 last save until July 14.

outside_scope_leads: All text was read. Epoch examples, every proposed network ownership mapping and all per-day subsidiary counts were not independently reproduced. The time spent by a maintainer cannot be measured from deletion timestamps.
review_limit: Assistant full-text reading and eight-question assessment, not independent human adjudication. Rejected artifacts retain their incomplete status. Source claims and qualified inferences are distinguished from independently observed outcomes. Incidental facts outside the eight-question scope are not exhaustively verified.
